tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)

    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)

    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.

    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

21	)
22	
23	func main() {
24		if err := run(); err != nil {
25			log.Fatal(err)
26		}
27	}
28	
29	func run() error {
30		databaseURL := os.Getenv("DATABASE_URL")
31		if databaseURL == "" {
32			return errors.New("DATABASE_URL environment variable is required")
33		}
34	
35		port := os.Getenv("PORT")
36		if port == "" {
37			port = "8080"
38		}
39	
40		if err := runMigrations(databaseURL); err != nil {
41			return fmt.Errorf("running migrations: %w", err)
42		}
43	
44		ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), syscall.SIGINT, syscall.SIGTERM)
45		defer stop()
46	
47		pool, err := pgxpool.New(ctx, databaseURL)
48		if err != nil {
49			return fmt.Errorf("creating pgxpool: %w", err)
50		}
51		defer pool.Close()
52	
53		repo := campaign.NewRepository(pool)
54		svc := campaign.NewService(repo)
55		h := campaign.NewHandler(svc)
56	
57		mux := http.NewServeMux()
58		mux.HandleFunc("POST /campaigns", h.Create)
59		mux.HandleFunc("GET /campaigns", h.List)
60		mux.HandleFunc("GET /campaigns/{id}", h.Get)
61		mux.HandleFunc("PATCH /campaigns/{id}", h.Update)
62		mux.HandleFunc("DELETE /campaigns/{id}", h.Delete)
63		mux.HandleFunc("POST /campaigns/{id}/pause", h.Pause)
64		mux.HandleFunc("POST /campaigns/{id}/resume", h.Resume)
65		mux.HandleFunc("POST /campaigns/{id}/end", h.End)
66		mux.HandleFunc("POST /impression/{id}", h.Impression)
67		mux.HandleFunc("GET /stats/{id}", h.Stats)
68	
69		server := &http.Server{
70			Addr:    ":" + port,
71			Handler: mux,
72		}
73	
74		errCh := make(chan error, 1)
75		go func() {
76			log.Printf("listening on :%s", port)
77			if err := server.ListenAndServe(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
78				errCh <- err
79			}
80		}()
81	
82		select {
83		case err := <-errCh:
84			return fmt.Errorf("server error: %w", err)
85		case <-ctx.Done():
86			log.Println("shutdown signal received")
87		}
88	
89		shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
90		defer cancel()
91		if err := server.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
92			return fmt.Errorf("server shutdown: %w", err)
93		}
94	
95		return nil
96	}
97	
98	func runMigrations(databaseURL string) error {
99		db, err := sql.Open("pgx", databaseURL)
100		if err != nil {
101			return fmt.Errorf("opening db for migrations: %w", err)
102		}
103		defer db.Close()

105		goose.SetBaseFS(migrations.FS)

107		if err := goose.SetDialect("postgres"); err != nil {

110	
111		if err := goose.Up(db, "."); err != nil {
112			return fmt.Errorf("goose up: %w", err)

1	package campaign
2	
3	import (
4		"context"
5		"time"
6	
7		"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool"
8	)
9	
10	type Repository struct {
11		pool *pgxpool.Pool
12	}
13	
14	func NewRepository(pool *pgxpool.Pool) *Repository {
15		return &Repository{pool: pool}
16	}
17	
18	const campaignColumns = "id, title, budget, spent, status, start_date, end_date, created_at, updated_at"
19	
20	func (r *Repository) Create(ctx context.Context, c Campaign) (Campaign, error) {
21		query := `
22			INSERT INTO campaigns (title, budget, start_date, end_date)
23			VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)
24			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
25	
26		var out Campaign
27		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, c.Title, c.Budget, c.StartDate, c.EndDate).Scan(
28			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
29			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
30		)
31		if err != nil {
32			return Campaign{}, err
33		}
34		return out, nil
35	}
36	
37	func (r *Repository) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Campaign, error) {
38		query := `
39			SELECT ` + campaignColumns + `
40			FROM campaigns
41			WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
42			ORDER BY created_at DESC`
43	
44		rows, err := r.pool.Query(ctx, query)
45		if err != nil {
46			return nil, err
47		}
48		defer rows.Close()
49	
50		campaigns := []Campaign{} // non-nil so a zero-row result marshals to [] not null
51		for rows.Next() {
52			var c Campaign
53			if err := rows.Scan(
54				&c.ID, &c.Title, &c.Budget, &c.Spent, &c.Status,
55				&c.StartDate, &c.EndDate, &c.CreatedAt, &c.UpdatedAt,
56			); err != nil {
57				return nil, err
58			}
59			campaigns = append(campaigns, c)
60		}
61		if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
62			return nil, err
63		}
64		return campaigns, nil
65	}
66	
67	func (r *Repository) GetByID(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Campaign, error) {
68		query := `
69			SELECT ` + campaignColumns + `
70			FROM campaigns
71			WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL`
72	
73		var c Campaign
74		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(
75			&c.ID, &c.Title, &c.Budget, &c.Spent, &c.Status,
76			&c.StartDate, &c.EndDate, &c.CreatedAt, &c.UpdatedAt,
77		)
78		if err != nil {
79			return Campaign{}, err
80		}
81		return c, nil
82	}
83	
84	// Update applies a partial update, using COALESCE so an absent (nil) field
85	// keeps the column's current value. Both invariants below are enforced as
86	// WHERE conditions rather than checked beforehand in Go, so they're evaluated
87	// by Postgres atomically against the current row under lock as part of this
88	// single statement — race-safe across multiple backend instances without any
89	// extra locking on our side:
90	//   - spent <= COALESCE(budget, budget): a no-op when budget isn't being
91	//     changed (spent <= budget already holds via the CHECK constraint), and
92	//     the real budget-decrease-vs-spent guard when it is.
93	//   - dates only touchable while paused: vacuously true when neither date
94	//     param is set, otherwise requires status = 'paused'.
95	//
96	// Zero matching rows surfaces as pgx.ErrNoRows via Scan, same as GetByID.
97	func (r *Repository) Update(ctx context.Context, id int64, title *string, budget *int64, startDate, endDate *time.Time) (Campaign, error) {
98		// Params are explicitly cast (::text/::bigint/::timestamptz) because when
99		// every optional field but one is nil, Postgres can't always infer a
100		// placeholder's type from COALESCE/IS NULL context alone and rejects the
101		// query with "could not determine data type of parameter" (42P08).
102		query := `
103			UPDATE campaigns
104			SET
105				title      = COALESCE($2::text, title),
106				budget     = COALESCE($3::bigint, budget),
107				start_date = COALESCE($4::timestamptz, start_date),
108				end_date   = COALESCE($5::timestamptz, end_date),
109				updated_at = now()
110			WHERE id = $1
111				AND deleted_at IS NULL
112				AND status <> 'completed'
113				AND spent <= COALESCE($3::bigint, budget)
114				AND (($4::timestamptz IS NULL AND $5::timestamptz IS NULL) OR status = 'paused')
115			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
116	
117		var out Campaign
118		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id, title, budget, startDate, endDate).Scan(
119			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
120			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
121		)
122		if err != nil {
123			return Campaign{}, err
124		}
125		return out, nil
126	}
127	
128	// SoftDelete never issues a DELETE statement — it sets deleted_at, and every
129	// query elsewhere filters deleted_at IS NULL. No status restriction: any
130	// non-deleted campaign, regardless of status, can be soft-deleted.
131	func (r *Repository) SoftDelete(ctx context.Context, id int64) error {
132		query := `
133			UPDATE campaigns
134			SET deleted_at = now(), updated_at = now()
135			WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL
136			RETURNING id`
137	
138		var returnedID int64
139		return r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(&returnedID)
140	}
141	
142	// Pause is the same conditional-UPDATE idiom as Update/Deduct: the WHERE
143	// clause is the sole enforcement mechanism, so zero matching rows surfaces
144	// as pgx.ErrNoRows and gets disambiguated by classifyUpdateConflict.
145	func (r *Repository) Pause(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Campaign, error) {
146		query := `
147			UPDATE campaigns
148			SET status = 'paused', updated_at = now()
149			WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status = 'active'
150			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
151	
152		var out Campaign
153		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(
154			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
155			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
156		)
157		if err != nil {
158			return Campaign{}, err
159		}
160		return out, nil
161	}
162	
163	// Resume: spent < budget and end_date > now() are evaluated by Postgres
164	// atomically against the current row as part of this one statement, so a
165	// concurrent impression exhausting the budget at the same instant can't
166	// race past this check — whichever statement runs first wins, and the other
167	// correctly sees the post-write state.
168	func (r *Repository) Resume(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Campaign, error) {
169		query := `
170			UPDATE campaigns
171			SET status = 'active', updated_at = now()
172			WHERE id = $1
173				AND deleted_at IS NULL
174				AND status = 'paused'
175				AND spent < budget
176				AND end_date > now()
177			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
178	
179		var out Campaign
180		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(
181			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
182			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
183		)
184		if err != nil {
185			return Campaign{}, err
186		}
187		return out, nil
188	}
189	
190	// End works from either 'active' or 'paused' — only 'completed' blocks it.
191	func (r *Repository) End(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Campaign, error) {
192		query := `
193			UPDATE campaigns
194			SET status = 'completed', updated_at = now()
195			WHERE id = $1 AND deleted_at IS NULL AND status <> 'completed'
196			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
197	
198		var out Campaign
199		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(
200			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
201			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
202		)
203		if err != nil {
204			return Campaign{}, err
205		}
206		return out, nil
207	}
208	
209	// Deduct atomically records one impression: increments spent by 1 and, if
210	// this deduction exhausts the budget, flips status to 'paused' in the same
211	// statement — no separate transition step, so no window where a concurrent
212	// call could sneak in between "deduct" and "pause". The WHERE clause is the
213	// sole correctness mechanism, evaluated by Postgres against the current row
214	// under lock as part of this one statement, so it's race-safe across
215	// multiple backend instances without any extra locking on our side.
216	func (r *Repository) Deduct(ctx context.Context, id int64) (Campaign, error) {
217		query := `
218			UPDATE campaigns
219			SET
220				spent  = spent + 1,
221				status = CASE WHEN spent + 1 >= budget THEN 'paused' ELSE status END,
222				updated_at = now()
223			WHERE id = $1
224				AND deleted_at IS NULL
225				AND status = 'active'
226				AND start_date <= now()
227				AND end_date > now()
228				AND spent < budget
229			RETURNING ` + campaignColumns
230	
231		var out Campaign
232		err := r.pool.QueryRow(ctx, query, id).Scan(
233			&out.ID, &out.Title, &out.Budget, &out.Spent, &out.Status,
234			&out.StartDate, &out.EndDate, &out.CreatedAt, &out.UpdatedAt,
235		)
236		if err != nil {
237			return Campaign{}, err
238		}
239		return out, nil
240	}

1	package campaign
2	
3	import (
4		"encoding/json"
5		"time"
6	)
7	
8	const (
9		StatusActive    = "active"
10		StatusPaused    = "paused"
11		StatusCompleted = "completed"
12	)
13	
14	type Campaign struct {
15		ID        int64     `json:"id"`
16		Title     string    `json:"title"`
17		Budget    int64     `json:"budget"`
18		Spent     int64     `json:"spent"`
19		Status    string    `json:"status"`
20		StartDate time.Time `json:"start_date"`
21		EndDate   time.Time `json:"end_date"`
22		CreatedAt time.Time `json:"created_at"`
23		UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
24	}
25	
26	// MarshalJSON adds a computed "remaining" field. Remaining budget is never
27	// stored (budget - spent), so it's derived here rather than on the struct.
28	func (c Campaign) MarshalJSON() ([]byte, error) {
29		type Alias Campaign // defined type, not an alias — drops MarshalJSON so this doesn't recurse
30	
31		// pgx returns scanned timestamps in the driver/host's local Location; the
32		// instant is correct but json's RFC3339 output would print that offset
33		// instead of "Z". Normalize to UTC here so every response is UTC.
34		c.StartDate = c.StartDate.UTC()
35		c.EndDate = c.EndDate.UTC()
36		c.CreatedAt = c.CreatedAt.UTC()
37		c.UpdatedAt = c.UpdatedAt.UTC()
38	
39		return json.Marshal(struct {
40			Alias
41			Remaining int64 `json:"remaining"`
42		}{
43			Alias:     Alias(c),
44			Remaining: c.Budget - c.Spent,
45		})
46	}
47	
48	type CreateInput struct {
49		Title     string      `json:"title"`
50		Budget    json.Number `json:"budget"`
51		StartDate time.Time   `json:"start_date"`
52		EndDate   time.Time   `json:"end_date"`
53	}
54	
55	// UpdateInput uses pointers so "field absent" (nil) is distinguishable from
56	// "field sent" — required for PATCH's partial-update semantics.
57	type UpdateInput struct {
58		Title     *string      `json:"title"`
59		Budget    *json.Number `json:"budget"`
60		StartDate *time.Time   `json:"start_date"`
61		EndDate   *time.Time   `json:"end_date"`
62	}
63	
64	// Stats is the smaller /stats/{id} shape (no title/dates/timestamps).
65	type Stats struct {
66		Impressions int64  `json:"impressions"`
67		Spent       int64  `json:"spent"`
68		Remaining   int64  `json:"remaining"`
69		Budget      int64  `json:"budget"`
70		Status      string `json:"status"`
71	}
72	
73	// Stats derives impressions from spent — impressions aren't stored as a
74	// separate counter, since 1 impression always equals 1 unit spent.
75	func (c Campaign) Stats() Stats {
76		return Stats{
77			Impressions: c.Spent,
78			Spent:       c.Spent,
79			Remaining:   c.Budget - c.Spent,
80			Budget:      c.Budget,
81			Status:      c.Status,
82		}
83	}

## Summary

Implemented the background sweep job:

- **`backend/internal/campaign/repository.go`** — `CompletePastEndDate` does one conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE deleted_at IS NULL AND status IN ('active','paused') AND end_date <= now()`, same idiom as the other WHERE-guarded updates.
- **`backend/internal/campaign/sweeper.go`** — new `Sweeper` type. `Run(ctx, interval)` sweeps once immediately (covers stale statuses after downtime), then loops on a `time.Ticker` until `ctx.Done()`. Logs only when rows are actually affected.
- **`backend/cmd/server/main.go`** — reads `SWEEP_INTERVAL` (Go duration string, e.g. `1m`, `30s`) via `time.ParseDuration`, defaulting to `time.Minute`; invalid values fail startup with a clear error. Sweeper runs in a goroutine on the same `ctx` as the HTTP server, so it stops on SIGINT/SIGTERM.
- **`.env.example`** — documented `SWEEP_INTERVAL=1m`.
- **`backend/internal/campaign/sweeper_test.go`** — new test against the Docker Compose Postgres: backdates one campaign's `end_date` via direct SQL (since `Create`/`Update` both reject past end dates by design), calls `CompletePastEndDate` directly, and asserts it flips to `completed` with `updated_at` advanced, while a still-current campaign is untouched.

Verified: `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean; `go test ./...` passes both the new sweeper test and the existing concurrency test; and I ran the actual server with `SWEEP_INTERVAL=2s`, inserted a live expired campaign via SQL, and watched the ticker log `sweep: marked 1 campaign(s) completed` and flip its status — confirming the wiring, not just the query, works.

input.content:
# Dockerize backend + frontend, make `docker compose up` self-sufficient

## Context

`docker-compose.yml` currently only runs Postgres — the backend and frontend
have to be started manually outside Docker, so a clean clone can't produce a
running system with one command. This adds a multi-stage `backend/Dockerfile`
and `frontend/Dockerfile`, an `nginx.conf` for the frontend that serves the
SPA and proxies `/api/*` to the backend (mirroring the existing Vite dev
proxy), and wires all three services together in `docker-compose.yml`. No
application code changes — infra files only.

## Research findings

- **Backend**: Go module at `backend/go.mod` (`go 1.27.1`), builds via
  `go build ./cmd/server`. Migrations are `//go:embed *.sql` in
  `backend/migrations/embed.go` — compiled into the binary, so the final
  image needs nothing but the binary itself. `main.go` reads `DATABASE_URL`,
  `PORT` (default 8080), `SWEEP_INTERVAL` (default 1m) from the environment.
  Pure Go deps (pgx, goose) — no CGO needed, so `CGO_ENABLED=0` produces a
  static binary alpine can run directly.
- **Frontend**: Vite + React, npm (`package-lock.json` present, no
  yarn/pnpm). Build script is `tsc -b && vite build` → output in `dist/`
  (confirmed by `frontend/.gitignore`). No `VITE_API_URL` or similar — every
  API call in `frontend/src/pages/*.tsx` goes through `frontend/src/api/client.ts`
  as a relative `fetch('/api/...')`. The dev proxy in `frontend/vite.config.ts`:
  ```ts
  '/api': { target: 'http://localhost:8080', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: p => p.replace(/^\/api/, '') }
  ```
  nginx must reproduce this exactly: strip `/api` and forward to the backend.
- **Env defaults**: root `.env` is gitignored; `.env.example` is the only
  tracked file. The existing `postgres` service already uses
  `${POSTGRES_USER:-campaign}`-style fallbacks so it works with no `.env`
  present at all — the new services must follow the same pattern so a clean
  clone with no `.env` still works.
- No existing Dockerfile, nginx.conf, or .dockerignore anywhere in the repo.

## Decisions from user

- Backend runtime base: **alpine** (not distroless) — keeps a shell for
  `docker exec` debugging, still small with `ca-certificates` added.
- Frontend host port: **80** — `docker compose up` then browse
  `http://localhost` with no port.
- Backend also publishes host port **8080** (explicit ask, for load-testing
  directly against the API).
- `frontend` depends on `backend` with the default `service_started`
  condition (no new `/health` endpoint added — out of scope, not requested).

## Files to add/change

### `backend/Dockerfile` (new)
Two stages:
1. `golang:1.27-alpine` builder — `COPY go.mod go.sum`, `go mod download`,
   `COPY . .`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -o /out/server ./cmd/server`.
   No separate copy step for `.sql` files — they're embedded at compile time
   from `backend/migrations/*.sql`, already present via `COPY . .`.
2. `alpine:3.20` runtime — `apk add --no-cache ca-certificates`, copy the
   binary in, `EXPOSE 8080`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/server"]`.

### `frontend/Dockerfile` (new)
Two stages:
1. `node:22-alpine` builder — `COPY package.json package-lock.json`,
   `npm ci`, `COPY . .`, `npm run build` (runs `tsc -b && vite build`,
   needs devDependencies, so no `--omit=dev`).
2. `nginx:1.27-alpine` runtime — copy `dist/` to
   `/usr/share/nginx/html`, copy `frontend/nginx.conf` to
   `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`, `EXPOSE 80`.

### `frontend/nginx.conf` (new)
```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;

    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    index index.html;

    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://backend:8080/;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location / {
        try_files $uri /index.html;
    }
}
```
`proxy_pass` with a trailing slash on both the `location` and the target URL
strips the `/api` prefix, same as the Vite `rewrite`. `try_files ... /index.html`
is the SPA fallback for client-side routes (`react-router`).

### `frontend/.dockerignore` (new)
```
node_modules
dist
dist-ssr
```
(No `backend/.dockerignore` — its build context has no committed bulky/local
output directories to exclude.)

### `docker-compose.yml` (edit)
Add `backend` and `frontend` services alongside the existing `postgres`:
```yaml
  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-campaign}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-campaign}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-campaign}?sslmode=disable
      PORT: 8080
      SWEEP_INTERVAL: ${SWEEP_INTERVAL:-1m}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    depends_on:
      - backend
```
Key point: `DATABASE_URL` here uses the Postgres **service name** (`postgres`)
as the host, not `localhost` — resolvable because compose puts all three
services on the same default network. This is separate from the existing
`.env`/`.env.example` `DATABASE_URL`, which stays as-is (`localhost:5432`)
since that one is for running the Go binary or `go test` directly on the
host against the Postgres container's published port.

### `.env.example` (no change needed)
Already has fallback-compatible values; nothing new required since compose
service defaults are inlined.

## Verification

1. `docker compose down -v` (clean slate — drops the `pgdata` volume so
   migrations run fresh) then `docker compose up --build`.
2. Confirm all three containers report healthy/running:
   `docker compose ps`.
3. Confirm the backend applied migrations and is reachable directly on the
   published port: `curl http://localhost:8080/campaigns` → `[]`.
4. Confirm the frontend serves the SPA and proxies the API through nginx
   with the `/api` prefix stripped:
   `curl http://localhost/` → HTML shell,
   `curl http://localhost/api/campaigns` → `[]` (same JSON as step 3).
5. Open `http://localhost` in a browser, create a campaign through the UI,
   and confirm it round-trips (proves the SPA fallback and the proxy both
   work for a real client-side-routed page load, not just curl).
6. `docker compose logs backend | grep sweep` after leaving it running past
   one `SWEEP_INTERVAL` tick — optional sanity check that the container's
   env vars (from earlier session's `SWEEP_INTERVAL` work) took effect.

# Dockerize backend + frontend, make `docker compose up` self-sufficient

## Context

`docker-compose.yml` currently only runs Postgres — the backend and frontend
have to be started manually outside Docker, so a clean clone can't produce a
running system with one command. This adds a multi-stage `backend/Dockerfile`
and `frontend/Dockerfile`, an `nginx.conf` for the frontend that serves the
SPA and proxies `/api/*` to the backend (mirroring the existing Vite dev
proxy), and wires all three services together in `docker-compose.yml`. No
application code changes — infra files only.

## Research findings

- **Backend**: Go module at `backend/go.mod` (`go 1.27.1`), builds via
  `go build ./cmd/server`. Migrations are `//go:embed *.sql` in
  `backend/migrations/embed.go` — compiled into the binary, so the final
  image needs nothing but the binary itself. `main.go` reads `DATABASE_URL`,
  `PORT` (default 8080), `SWEEP_INTERVAL` (default 1m) from the environment.
  Pure Go deps (pgx, goose) — no CGO needed, so `CGO_ENABLED=0` produces a
  static binary alpine can run directly.
- **Frontend**: Vite + React, npm (`package-lock.json` present, no
  yarn/pnpm). Build script is `tsc -b && vite build` → output in `dist/`
  (confirmed by `frontend/.gitignore`). No `VITE_API_URL` or similar — every
  API call in `frontend/src/pages/*.tsx` goes through `frontend/src/api/client.ts`
  as a relative `fetch('/api/...')`. The dev proxy in `frontend/vite.config.ts`:
  ```ts
  '/api': { target: 'http://localhost:8080', changeOrigin: true, rewrite: p => p.replace(/^\/api/, '') }
  ```
  nginx must reproduce this exactly: strip `/api` and forward to the backend.
- **Env defaults**: root `.env` is gitignored; `.env.example` is the only
  tracked file. The existing `postgres` service already uses
  `${POSTGRES_USER:-campaign}`-style fallbacks so it works with no `.env`
  present at all — the new services must follow the same pattern so a clean
  clone with no `.env` still works.
- No existing Dockerfile, nginx.conf, or .dockerignore anywhere in the repo.

## Decisions from user

- Backend runtime base: **alpine** (not distroless) — keeps a shell for
  `docker exec` debugging, still small with `ca-certificates` added.
- Frontend host port: **80** — `docker compose up` then browse
  `http://localhost` with no port.
- Backend also publishes host port **8080** (explicit ask, for load-testing
  directly against the API).
- `frontend` depends on `backend` with the default `service_started`
  condition (no new `/health` endpoint added — out of scope, not requested).

## Files to add/change

### `backend/Dockerfile` (new)
Two stages:
1. `golang:1.27-alpine` builder — `COPY go.mod go.sum`, `go mod download`,
   `COPY . .`, `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -o /out/server ./cmd/server`.
   No separate copy step for `.sql` files — they're embedded at compile time
   from `backend/migrations/*.sql`, already present via `COPY . .`.
2. `alpine:3.20` runtime — `apk add --no-cache ca-certificates`, copy the
   binary in, `EXPOSE 8080`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/server"]`.

### `frontend/Dockerfile` (new)
Two stages:
1. `node:22-alpine` builder — `COPY package.json package-lock.json`,
   `npm ci`, `COPY . .`, `npm run build` (runs `tsc -b && vite build`,
   needs devDependencies, so no `--omit=dev`).
2. `nginx:1.27-alpine` runtime — copy `dist/` to
   `/usr/share/nginx/html`, copy `frontend/nginx.conf` to
   `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`, `EXPOSE 80`.

### `frontend/nginx.conf` (new)
```nginx
server {
    listen 80;
    server_name _;

    root /usr/share/nginx/html;
    index index.html;

    location /api/ {
        proxy_pass http://backend:8080/;
        proxy_http_version 1.1;
        proxy_set_header Host $host;
        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
    }

    location / {
        try_files $uri /index.html;
    }
}
```
`proxy_pass` with a trailing slash on both the `location` and the target URL
strips the `/api` prefix, same as the Vite `rewrite`. `try_files ... /index.html`
is the SPA fallback for client-side routes (`react-router`).

### `frontend/.dockerignore` (new)
```
node_modules
dist
dist-ssr
```
(No `backend/.dockerignore` — its build context has no committed bulky/local
output directories to exclude.)

### `docker-compose.yml` (edit)
Add `backend` and `frontend` services alongside the existing `postgres`:
```yaml
  backend:
    build:
      context: ./backend
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://${POSTGRES_USER:-campaign}:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-campaign}@postgres:5432/${POSTGRES_DB:-campaign}?sslmode=disable
      PORT: 8080
      SWEEP_INTERVAL: ${SWEEP_INTERVAL:-1m}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy

  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "80:80"
    depends_on:
      - backend
```
Key point: `DATABASE_URL` here uses the Postgres **service name** (`postgres`)
as the host, not `localhost` — resolvable because compose puts all three
services on the same default network. This is separate from the existing
`.env`/`.env.example` `DATABASE_URL`, which stays as-is (`localhost:5432`)
since that one is for running the Go binary or `go test` directly on the
host against the Postgres container's published port.

### `.env.example` (no change needed)
Already has fallback-compatible values; nothing new required since compose
service defaults are inlined.

## Verification

1. `docker compose down -v` (clean slate — drops the `pgdata` volume so
   migrations run fresh) then `docker compose up --build`.
2. Confirm all three containers report healthy/running:
   `docker compose ps`.
3. Confirm the backend applied migrations and is reachable directly on the
   published port: `curl http://localhost:8080/campaigns` → `[]`.
4. Confirm the frontend serves the SPA and proxies the API through nginx
   with the `/api` prefix stripped:

   work for a real client-side-routed page load, not just curl).
6. `docker compose logs backend | grep sweep` after leaving it running past
   one `SWEEP_INTERVAL` tick — optional sanity check that the container's
   env vars (from earlier session's `SWEEP_INTERVAL` work) took effect.

## Summary

Implemented per the approved plan — no application code touched, only infra:

- **`backend/Dockerfile`** — `golang:1.27-alpine` build stage → static binary → `alpine:3.20` + `ca-certificates` runtime
- **`backend/.dockerignore`** — mirrors `.gitignore`'s local-artifact patterns
- **`frontend/Dockerfile`** — `node:22-alpine` build stage (`npm ci && npm run build`) → `nginx:1.27-alpine` serving `dist/`
- **`frontend/.dockerignore`** — excludes `node_modules`, `dist`, `dist-ssr`
- **`frontend/nginx.conf`** — proxies `/api/*` to `backend:8080` with the prefix stripped (mirrors the Vite dev proxy), SPA fallback via `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html`
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — added `backend` (depends on `postgres` with `condition: service_healthy`, publishes `8080`) and `frontend` (publishes `3000:80`, depends on `backend`)

**Verified live**: `docker compose down -v && docker compose up --build -d` brought up all three services from a completely clean volume; migrations ran automatically; `curl localhost:8080/campaigns` and `curl localhost:3000/api/campaigns` both returned `[]`; a POST through the frontend proxy created a real campaign; a client-side route (`/campaigns/999`) correctly fell back to the SPA shell instead of 404ing. Cleaned up the test campaign afterward.

The stack is still running — `docker compose down` when you're done, or `docker compose down -v` to also drop the Postgres volume.
